plan.topic: Tirzepatide plus ixekizumab for psoriatic arthritis with obesity: the TOGETHER-PsA randomized Phase 3b trial, presented at ACR Convergence 2026 (6–11 Nov)
plan.angle: Evergreen framing: 'Tirzepatide and Psoriatic Arthritis: What a Trial Found' (don't call it new). Open: 'In a randomized trial in adults with active psoriatic arthritis and overweight or obesity, adding tirzepatide to the arthritis drug ixekizumab was compared with ixekizumab alone.' Credit: 'TOGETHER-PsA, Arthritis & Rheumatology, 2026; open-label, company-funded'. No ACR Convergence attribution. Give 138 vs 133 people, week 36, the composite (ACR50 plus at least 10% weight loss) 31.7% vs 0.8%, and ACR50 alone 33.5% vs 20.4%. Week-52 figures go in only if confirmed from a primary Lilly release or abstract, labelled as conference/company-reported. Keep: one trial; tirzepatide isn't approved to treat psoriatic arthritis; weight is one measure among joint outcomes; the qualitative GI line; 'Don't switch, stop or change your medicines on your own; talk to your rheumatologist or prescriber'; the Exp F line, 'Not personal advice' and the prescriber line; loop to the opening.
plan.working_title: Tirzepatide and Psoriatic Arthritis: What a Trial Found
plan.why: It's a fresh randomized, tirzepatide-named result presented at ACR this week, with very little creator coverage. It fills the playbook's 13:00 fresh-randomized-result slot and the 'benefits beyond weight' pillar. | fact-check: The trial is real, but the brief gets its status wrong. TOGETHER-PsA is a Phase 3b, randomized, OPEN-LABEL, 52-week trial. Topline results came out in January 2026. It was presented as a late-breaker at AAD in March 2026 and is already PEER-REVIEWED in Arthritis & Rheumatology 2026 (doi:10.1002/art.70134). Week-52 data were reported in September 2026. So 'presented at ACR Convergence 2026', 'fresh randomized result' and 'company-reported, not yet peer-reviewed' are all inaccurate. The craft notes also bar calling it 'new' because the data are more than 3 months old. It doesn't meet the 13:00 'fresh randomized result' criterion. The scheduler should know this, and could run it as an evergreen Short or move it to a slot where freshness isn't required. Confirmed facts: 271 adults with active PsA and BMI ≥30, or BMI 27–29.9 plus at least one weight-related condition (so say 'overweight or obesity', not 'obesity'). Arms: ixekizumab + tirzepatide n=138 vs ixekizumab alone n=133. Primary composite at week 36: ACR50 (at least a 50% improvement in arthritis signs and symptoms) AND ≥10% weight reduction, 31.7% vs 0.8%. ACR50 alone at week 36: 33.5% vs 20.4%. Weight is half of the composite, so the 31.7% vs 0.8% gap mostly reflects the weight half. Pair it with the ACR50-alone figure so the joint benefit isn't overstated. Per-arm GI rates weren't found in the secondary sources. Use a qualitative GI line ('stomach side effects such as nausea were more common with tirzepatide') unless the paper's per-arm figures are opened and confirmed. Sources checked: https://www.healio.com/news/rheumatology/20260609/taltz-plus-tirzepatide-superior-to-monotherapy-in-psoriatic-arthritis-alongside-obesity ; https://www.dermatologytimes.com/view/eli-lilly-trial-shows-superior-outcomes-with-ixekizumab-and-tirzepatide-in-patients-with-psa-and-obesity ; https://www.hcplive.com/view/xekizumab-tirzepatide-sustains-1-year-gains-psoriatic-disease-obesity

package.title: Tirzepatide + Psoriatic Arthritis: What a Trial Found #shorts
package.description:
One randomized trial: adults with active psoriatic arthritis and overweight or obesity took ixekizumab; 138 added tirzepatide, 133 didn't. Week 36, both goals (at least 50% arthritis improvement plus at least 10% weight loss): 31.7% with tirzepatide added vs 0.8% without. Joint goal alone (a secondary result): 33.5% with tirzepatide added vs 20.4% without. Most common side effects with tirzepatide added: nausea, diarrhoea, constipation and injection site reactions. One open-label, company-funded trial. Tirzepatide isn't approved for psoriatic arthritis.
Sources:
Arthritis Rheumatol 2026 (TOGETHER-PsA): https://digitalcommons.providence.org/publications_2/257
Healio: https://www.healio.com/news/rheumatology/20260609/taltz-plus-tirzepatide-superior-to-monotherapy-in-psoriatic-arthritis-alongside-obesity
Zepbound label: https://pi.lilly.com/us/zepbound-uspi.pdf
#Tirzepatide #PsoriaticArthritis #GLP1 #ClinicalTrial
Not personal advice. Don't switch, stop or change your medicines on your own. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

Psoriatic arthritis plus extra weight is exhausting on its own. One randomized trial looked at tackling both at once.

Adults with active psoriatic arthritis and overweight or obesity who took the arthritis drug ixekizumab either added tirzepatide or didn't.

• Tirzepatide isn't approved for psoriatic arthritis.

If you're managing psoriatic arthritis and extra weight, you know how much harder each one makes the other feel. One randomized trial looked at tackling both together.

In the TOGETHER-PsA Phase 3b trial, adults with active psoriatic arthritis and overweight or obesity who took the biologic ixekizumab (Taltz) either added tirzepatide or stuck with ixekizumab alone. It's one open-label, company-funded trial, and common side effects with tirzepatide added included nausea, diarrhoea, constipation and injection site reactions. Tirzepatide isn't approved for psoriatic arthritis.

factcheck.summary: The script is accurate. Every number matches TOGETHER-PsA (Merola et al., Arthritis Rheumatol 2026, DOI 10.1002/art.70134): 271 adults randomized 138 vs 133. On the primary endpoint at week 36 (ACR50 plus at least 10% weight loss), 31.7% reached it with tirzepatide added vs 0.8% on ixekizumab alone (P<0.001). On the secondary ACR50-alone result, it was 33.5% vs 20.4% (P=0.02). The population matches the trial: BMI 30 or higher, or BMI 27–29.9 with at least one weight-related condition. The open-label (assessor-blinded) design and Lilly sponsorship are confirmed by Healio, Dermatology Times and the Lilly press release. The script is honest about scope: it separates the composite result from the joint-only result, says "one open-label, company-funded trial" and "not approved for psoriatic arthritis", and speaks and shows all three safety lines. Four minor fixes: (1) the side-effect line makes a comparison the sources don't give; (2) the src5 description credits a statement to the press release that it doesn't contain; (3) the on-screen stat text in s3 and s4 doesn't name the two groups; (4) the Short leaves out the standard last line.

issues.claim: Stomach side effects such as nausea were more common with tirzepatide added.
issues.problem: The sources (Lilly press release, Dermatology Times) only list the most common adverse events (≥5%) in each arm. With tirzepatide added: nausea, diarrhoea, constipation and injection site reactions. Ixekizumab alone: injection site reactions and upper respiratory infections. They give no rates by arm, so 'more common' is a comparison the source doesn't state.
issues.fix: Narration: "One open-label, company-funded trial. With tirzepatide added, the most common side effects were nausea, diarrhoea, constipation and injection site reactions. Tirzepatide isn't approved for psoriatic arthritis." List item 2: "Most common with tirzepatide added: nausea, diarrhoea, constipation, injection site reactions"

issues.claim: Press release covers '...adverse events by arm, not approved for PsA'
issues.problem: The press release doesn't say tirzepatide isn't approved for PsA. It says Zepbound is approved for obesity and Taltz for PsA. The 'not approved' line is backed by the label's indications (src4), not by src5.
issues.fix: Change the src5 title to: "Lilly's Taltz (ixekizumab) and Zepbound (tirzepatide) used together delivered superior efficacy in first-of-its-kind Phase 3b trial (press release, 8 Jan 2026)". Remove src5 from the s5 'not approved' item and keep src4 as the source for it.

notes: Automated audit confirms the "Joints" tag and the "Weight" tag overlap each other and the caption text "ten percent weight loss" at 25.6s.
A body-outline figure with a crying, sweating bone face for a hopeful line ("Half my pain gone?") sends a mixed emotional signal.
Caption card "SMALLER —" ends on a dash, breaking the no-trailing-punctuation caption rule and leaving the sentence visibly unfinished.
The small heart icon in the corner is tiny and nearly lost against the teal background.
Caption "THIS WAS ONE OPEN-LABEL," ends on a comma, and the automated audit shows it overlapping the next card "the most common" at 53.99s.
The red question-mark icon and the small doctor icon float with no clear focal hierarchy against an empty clipboard illustration.
Automated audit confirms the "Stomach" tag overlaps the captions "side effects were nausea, diarrhoea," and "constipation, and injection site reactio[ns]" at 56.46s and 59.47s.
Caption "SIDE EFFECTS WERE NAUSEA, DIARRHOEA," ends on a comma mid-list, which reads as cut off.
Four chips stacked at the very top plus a body/stomach label is a lot of simultaneous text for one shot.
A blue shield with a green checkmark (a universally positive/approved icon) is used to illustrate "not approved," which reads as the opposite of the intended meaning at a glance.
Caption "AND TIRZEPATIDE ISN'T" ends on a contraction/auxiliary verb, splitting the sentence awkwardly.
Caption card "TIRZEPATIDE QUESTION FROM THE" ends on the article "THE," an explicit broken-caption violation, and the sentence is cut off mid-thought.
Speech bubble reads "Full story's in the link!" while the caption reads "FULL BREAKDOWN ON OUR CHANNEL," — two different wordings for the same closing line, and the caption ends on a comma, cut off.
Unlinked anchor/selection handles are visible around the heart and arrow, suggesting a leftover editor artifact wasn't cleared before render.

audio.soundNotes: Music is already sitting right in the target window (-13.5 dB under voice, -14.2 in pauses), so left at 1.0x. The two biggest problems were density and a few over-loud pops: the "138 vs 133" stat reveal around 13.6-13.9s had nine overlapping stock SFX in under 0.3s — trimmed to three (opening pop, one soft pop, one ding accent) and killed the redundant tick/extra pops/swooshes. Also silenced several duplicate pop+whoosh or swell+tick pairs firing at the exact same timestamp throughout (28, 39, 44, 48, 54, 58, 63, 68) since one sound reads the same as two and frees up headroom. Pulled down two speech-time cues that were ringing far louder than the voice (i30 at -8.3dB during narration, i43 at -12.6dB) to sit inside the -14/-20dB "felt not heard" zone. Added a quiet somber piano note under the "not approved" caution beat to mark the tonal pivot without extra noise, and a tiny paper-rustle under the trial-label reveal for texture.
